mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.measurement: The single shared starter exit-hazard model for every pitcher prop and window (strikeouts, outs, earned runs/hits/walks, F5, inherited runners, win credit). Discrete-time logistic hazard h(b) = P(removed after batter b | still in) estimated on 5 seasons of starts (regular season; separate postseason intercept). Predictors: batters faced b (spline, knots at 9, 18, 27), third-trip indicator I(b >= 19), inning-boundary indicator I(batter b made the third out of an inning), pitch count (spline), runs allowed so far (0,1,2,3+), runners on at b, team lead/deficit bucket (leading, tied or trailing by <=2, trailing by >=3), days rest, season-to-date average pitches per start (shrunk to league with k = 8 starts), manager random effect (shrunk, k = 40 starts; reset when the manager changes), bullpen-freshness index (relievers used last 2 days); an announced pitch cap from mlb.pitch_count_limit enters as a hard truncation (h = 1 once the cap is reached). Output: survival S(b) for b = 1..36, E[BF] = sum S(b), and, run inside the PA simulation with outs per batter, the distribution of outs at exit. mlb.sp_workload, mlb.exit_boundary_mass and mlb.leash are readouts or components of this model and are not fitted separately. As-of: manager and pitcher effects fit through the prior game; game-state predictors enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data.

mlb.exit_boundary_mass.label: Exit-outs lattice readout of the shared starter exit hazard: P(removal at outs = j | reached), including the spikes at inning boundaries
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.mechanism: Starter removals cluster at inning boundaries and at the start of the third time through; this lattice is read off the one shared exit-hazard model rather than estimated as a separate model, so outs, strikeout and earned-run ladders of the same start stay consistent.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.measurement: Not fitted separately. Simulate the start with mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve (which carries the inning-boundary, third-trip, pitch-count and run-state terms and the manager effect) inside the plate-appearance simulation, mapping batters faced to outs with mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning; record exit_outs in each of 20,000 simulated starts. Output f(j) = share of simulations ending with exactly j outs for j = 0..27, g_j = f(j) / P(outs >= j), and P(outs >= m). Diagnostic only: compare g_j with the manager's empirical exit lattice over the last 4 seasons (cells of pitch-count bucket <85, 85-100, >100 x run-state bucket, shrunk to league with k = 30 starts); persistent gaps are fixed by adding terms to the shared hazard, never by a second model. As-of: games through the previous day.

mlb.sp_workload.measurement: Readout of the shared exit hazard mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve, not a separate model: the distribution of batters faced is P(BF = b) = S(b-1) * h(b) with E[BF] = sum over b of S(b); outs and pitch-count distributions come from the same hazard run inside the plate-appearance simulation (pitches per PA from mlb.sp_efficiency and mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa; announced caps from mlb.pitch_count_limit). The pitcher's last 10-15 starts (excluding injury-shortened) enter only through the hazard's pitcher terms. Output E[BF], E[outs], E[pitches] and their distributions. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.leash.label: Manager hook tendency (component of the shared starter exit hazard: manager effect and bullpen freshness)
mlb.leash.measurement: Not a separate model: leash is reported as the manager random effect (shrunk with k = 40 starts, reset on a manager change) and the bullpen-freshness coefficient inside mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve, summarised as the manager's predicted median batters faced at exit for a league-average starter at 0 runs allowed and a 95-pitch count, relative to the league median. Units: batters faced relative to league. As-of: starts through the previous day.

mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.measurement: P(exit with k runners) from the shared exit hazard mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve evaluated inside the PA simulation x P(each inherited runner scores | reliever profile) with reliever strand rate shrunk to league (k = 60 BF with inherited runners). Expected extra ER = sum_k P(k) x k x p_score x (1-unearned share). Use the likely first reliever from bullpen availability (setup man or long man). Units: expected earned runs added. As-of: lineup post + bullpen usage from prior 2 days.

mlb.f5_reliever_innings_share.measurement: From the shared starter exit hazard mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve compute E[outs by reliever in innings 1-5] = 15 - E[min(starter outs, 15)]; relief quality from the likely first reliever and leverage; F5 reliever share = that/15. F5 runs = starter rate x share_starter + reliever rate x share_relief. Uses 5 seasons start logs, k = 8 starts shrinkage to team average. Units: outs and runs per out. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.measurement: Pitcher barrel%/FB% allowed by batter hand, HR/FB regressed (prior weight ~200 FB); combine with hitter HR profile via log5 for per-PA HR probability. When used for opposing-hitter markets before first pitch (single-game HR, hits, TB), evaluate it as a mixture over starters: per-PA HR probability = (1 - P(change)) * p(announced starter) + P(change) * sum over replacements r of P(r | change) * p(r), with P(change) and the replacement distribution (next rotation arm, opener plus bulk, bullpen game) from mlb.f5_starter_change_risk at the same as-of time; for the pitcher's own ladders use the announced pitcher only. As-of: lineup post.

mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.mechanism: Contracts that do not gate on the pitcher (F5 lines, opposing-hitter props) stay live when the listed starter is scratched or swapped, so the change probability and the replacement's identity shift the whole outcome distribution.
mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.measurement: P(change) = logistic(a + b1*days_to_first_pitch + b2*IL_return_flag + b3*injury_report_flag + b4*team opener or bulk start rate in last 10 starts + b5*postseason + b6*doubleheader), fitted only on own-captured announced-versus-actual starters; until at least one full season of captured vintages exists, use the league base rate stratified by status flags with a Beta prior (k = 100 games) and label the output uncalibrated. Replacement distribution = mixture of next-in-rotation, bulk reliever and opener with their F5 run rates over 2 seasons shrunk to team average with k = 8 starts. Output P(change), the replacement distribution (identity, throwing hand and role of each candidate with probabilities), E[F5 runs | change] minus E[F5 runs | no change] for F5 markets, and the replacement mixture used by opposing-hitter props through mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability. As-of: each timestamp before first pitch, using only announcements available then.

mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.label: Manager of the Year score: wins over preseason expectation, division outcome and turnaround
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.mechanism: BBWAA voters choose Manager of the Year before the postseason on team surprise and success relative to preseason expectation rather than on absolute record; the executive award has a different electorate and its own input.

mlb.award_narrative.label: Award narrative flags: pre-registered milestone, comeback, first-year, positional-scarcity and team-surprise indicators
mlb.award_narrative.measurement: Binary flags per candidate-season tagged from official season statistics at the ballot deadline (end of the regular season), never from media text: milestone = reached a pre-registered threshold (50 HR, 200 hits, 40 SB with 40 HR, 20 wins, ERA under 2.00 with 162 IP, 300 strikeouts, 40 saves, .350 AVG qualified); comeback = prior-season fWAR <= 0.5 or prior-season PA < 200 (IP < 60 for pitchers) with current fWAR >= 3; first_year = first season in MLB or in the league after a cross-league trade before July; positional_scarcity = primary position C, SS or CF with fWAR rank in the top 3 at that position; team_surprise = team wins minus preseason projected wins (mean of ZiPS and PECOTA) >= 8. Flags enter mlb.award_vote_rank_model as additive terms in the worth function with coefficients fitted per electorate class and ridge-shrunk toward 0 (penalty 3 seasons); report the incremental log-likelihood of each flag over WAR and team success on 1996-2025 ballots and drop flags with no gain. Sources: Baseball-Reference/FanGraphs season and career tables, preseason projection archives.
mlb.award_narrative.mechanism: Voters respond to storylines and team success beyond raw metrics; the storylines are encoded as pre-registered flags computed from official statistics so their effect can be estimated per electorate.
mlb.award_narrative.rationale: A candidate with the best WAR on a non-playoff team may lose to one on a playoff team, and milestone or comeback seasons draw votes beyond their WAR. Subtle: narrative must be operationalised as fixed, statistics-based flags tagged at the ballot deadline (never media mentions or free text), and its incremental effect over WAR and team success may be small, so each flag is kept only if it adds likelihood.

mlb.award_vote_rank_model.measurement: Plackett-Luce likelihood on 1996-2025 BBWAA ballots per award and league (rank-ordered top 10 for MVP with points 14-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1, top 5 for Cy Young since 2010 with 7-4-3-2-1, top 3 for Rookie and Manager of the Year with 5-3-1): worth_i = exp(b1*WAR_z + b2*team_win_pct_z + b3*counting_z + b4*playoff_flag + b5*milestone_flag + position/pitcher effects), z-scores computed within each league-season over the top 15 candidates by WAR, WAR = mean of fWAR and bWAR at the end of the regular season (ballot deadline). Estimate by maximum likelihood with ridge shrinkage of each award's coefficients toward the pooled coefficients of the same electorate class from mlb.award_electorate_procedure (penalty equal to 3 seasons of data); BBWAA coefficients are never pooled with panel, beat-reporter, fan or executive awards. Simulate 30 voter ballots from the fitted model (temperature tau fitted on first-place-vote dispersion) with the real points scale; output P(winner) and P(top 3 by points). milestone_flag and the other narrative terms are the pre-registered flags of mlb.award_narrative. As-of: final regular-season stats, before ballot release.

mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.label: Per-PA base-out state distribution from the confirmed lineup (Markov chain), with RBI opportunity ahead and run-scoring probability behind each hitter
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.mechanism: The same lineup Markov chain gives both legs of a hitter's run production: the runners and outs he finds when he bats (RBI opportunity, from the hitters ahead) and the chance he comes around to score after reaching base (from the hitters behind him).
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.rationale: Average RBI and run opportunity per slot hides lineup-specific variation: the same cleanup hitter has materially more RBI chances behind two .380-OBP hitters than behind two .300-OBP hitters, and a leadoff hitter scores far more often with power bats behind him; KXMLBRBI uses the first output and KXMLBHRR needs both, so one shared chain keeps the hits and RBI archetypes consistent.
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.measurement: Markov chain over 24 transient base-out states (8 base occupancy sets x 0/1/2 outs) plus the inning-end absorbing state, with per-batter outcome probabilities (1B, 2B, 3B, HR, BB/HBP, K, GIDP, other out, reach on error) from batter rates shrunk to league with k = 200 PA, log5-adjusted to the starter (first 2.5 times through) then bullpen, with park multiplier. Runner advancement probabilities from league event data by outcome and base-out state. Solve analytically across the 9-slot order for 9 innings. Outputs for each batter's n-th PA: (a) the distribution of (runners on base, outs) when he bats and expected runners on base (RBI leg); (b) for each way he can end the PA on base (1B, 2B, 3B, BB/HBP, ROE) the probability he later scores in that inning, computed by continuing the chain from the resulting base-out state with the following batters' outcome probabilities and tracking his runner position (runs leg), so P(run | PA n) = P(HR) + sum over on-base outcomes o of P(o) x P(score | o, state); and (c) expected runs scored per PA. Units: runners per PA, probabilities, runs per PA. As-of: lineup post.
